A position is 'where', and a point is 'the place it marks'. This distinction comes from the compressed layer (L2), not the original, and the unfolding passes it on.

new_possibilities: The [guess] tags are a free diagnostic. The blind unfolding marks exactly where the compression cut through to the bone (root node, script per station, extends line, the full _ready bodies, which value to restore, why there is a feeler). Each [guess] could become a test that L3 has to pass.

A 'gives' gate. Every stuck point about code (':=', '.new()', 'add_child', what 'returned' means) is a term L2 declares under 'gives:' but never defines in a sentence. A check that each 'gives' term has one defining line in its section would turn the type-safety idea into something a tool can enforce. The reverse check is a used-but-not-given list: museum, label, extends, Debug.
The parenting tree in 1.3 (Solid -> marker, Solid -> solid -> collider) shows C76/C77 at a glance, more compactly than either the original prose or the code. It is worth adding to the original.

'Why do the white sphere and its boundary line up exactly? Because both are built from the same two variables.' This turns C82 from something sitting silently in the code into a question the student can answer. The original leaves it in the code.
Tying 1.4 back to 1.3 ('the light changes what is seen, not what is touched') makes the lesson a three-way split: seen, touched, lit. The original never names that split.

A possible new experiment, from the note on SphereMesh height: set sphere.height on its own, apart from radius. It is another disagreement between two numbers that look like one, and it parallels the mesh/shape disagreement.
A small observable that confirms 'a value alone does nothing': the unused-variable warning appears in position.gd and disappears in visible.gd once point_position is used.

The reader put 'only' back ('Change only the shape's radius') and reconstructed the 'visible gap'. Some forces come back from context, so they can stay compressed. Others, like the reason the feeler exists and the independence of the probe, did not come back and must be kept.
lost_vectors: Direction, from appearing to crossing. The original frames the lesson from the viewer: 'The supplied scene already gives us a floor, a light and a view. We will keep those while changing what appears in front of us.' L2 replaces this with 'You change the three scripts: what a feeler can cross', and the unfolding hardens it to 'Everything you change ... changes one thing'. The visible axis loses its own direction: 'We can change how much the sphere hides without changing what can pass through it' collapses into 'a mesh is not touched'. Hiding was a second dimension, and it is gone.

Connection, from the instrument to the thing measured. 'It belongs to the supplied test, not to the position we have just defined' was cut. The reader filled the gap with a different cause (there is no body there), which is physically plausible but is the wrong lesson. This is the only quiz question answered flat wrong.

Connection, from the shortcut to the system it must enter. The original's restore is an expression: 'Restore sphere_shape.radius = radius.' The literal 0.35 is a shortcut that cuts the shape off from the shared variable, and restoring it puts the shape back into the system. L2 says 'Restore 0.14', a value instead of a link, so the coupling that makes surface and boundary agree is no longer what gets restored. The same happens to 'Its height follows because the script makes it twice the radius': L2 leaves that link silent inside the code.

Force of the withheld. 'For now, this is the supplied position at our station. Point Coordinates will make its three components the subject of a lesson.' This is a deliberate dark spot with a promise attached. L2 drops both, and the blind reader fills the dark spot with x/y/z and metres. That forecloses the next lesson's subject, which is the clearest case of an unfolding guessing into space the original kept open on purpose.

Force of the rhythm. The original ends every experiment by restoring what it changed (1.12; the height; radius 0.14; sphere_shape.radius = radius; both radii to 0.14). L2 keeps one ambiguous 'Restore 0.14', so the 1.2 experiments now build on each other (radius 0.3 on top of height 1.7), and the 0.3/0.07 trial starts from 0.35. The method of always returning to the matching default is gone.

Connection, from why there is a feeler. 'The fixed-camera study supplies another moving body so we can test the same relation.' L2 jumps straight to 'In the museum, your own movement meets them', with no bridge. The reader guessed the bridge and was unsure.

Direction of the ending: from opening to closure. 'The large sphere at the end of the museum corridor asks us to return to those choices ... Knowing its construction gives us another way to change the encounter' became 'you know how to rebuild it'. An invitation to vary the encounter became a certificate that you can reproduce the object.

Hierarchy of evidence. 'The contact test works without that overlay' was cut. The Debug overlay becomes a flat fact, the reader treats it as part of the procedure in Q10, and the feeler loses its place as the primary witness.

A word changed type. The original keeps 'marker is the node that displays it' apart from 'the physics body'. L2's type line 'body: a node you place' applies 'body' to both marker and solid. For a text that claims type safety, this is the one place where a name's meaning did not stay fixed.

Truth of a quantifier. 'This is the whole script' was true in the original because extends Node3D was shown. In L2, 'That is all of position.gd' sits under two lines, so the claim became false. Compression cut the referent and kept the quantifier.

Smaller losses. The fill light ('a dim fill leaves the spheres visible' became 'spheres dim'). The scope boundary ('The portable study keeps its supplied light. Building the switch ... is outside this lesson.'). The construction reference and its 'without adding another required exercise'. 'Then reads its movement' in the next-lesson line. The analogy 'borrowed equipment, like the camera'. The sweep repeating.
readability: Dense but mostly decodable: 25 stuck points and 12/16 on the quiz. The misses sit where a sentence of reason was cut (Q3 the probe's independence, Q13-14 the deferral and the construction reference), not where code was shortened. Code came back almost perfectly. The friction comes from 'gives' terms that are declared but never defined (:=, .new(), add_child, 'returned'), fragments presented as wholes ('That is all of position.gd'), poetic lines that need decoding ('empty space resists', 'about one centre', 'a point to hold'), the author-facing HTML comments, and a museum that neither L2 nor the original ever introduces. That last stuck point is inherited from the original, not caused by the compression.
